newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Eregli hits steel output targets.
newsitem.headline: Turk Eregli hits steel output targets.

text.p: Turkey's biggest flat steel producer, largely state-owned Eregli Demir ve Celik Fabrikalari A.S. exceeded its export target by 30 percent and met its domestic sales target in the first five months of 1997, a senior company official said.

"We exported 274,000 tonnes of steel in five months which was 30 percent above our target and we met our domestic target with 861,000 tonnes sold in the same period," Isik Eyuboglu, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Eregli's five-month export revenue was $85.36 million. The company produced 1,175,000 tonnes of steel in January-May and sold 1,135,000 tonnes of it.
Shares of the company eased to 18,000 lira at midday on Friday from Thursday's 18,500 close as the market index plunged 4.06 percent in the first session.
Eregli aims to sell 2.85 million tonnes of steel this year, including 500,000 tonnes to be exported. Its main export markets are Italy, England, Spain, the U.S. and Israel.
The company produced 2.621 million tonnes of flat steel in 1996 when its sales totalled 2.517 million tonnes, including 502,000 tonnes of exports.

Eyuboglu pointed out that the company's end-1997 sales target could be exceeded thanks to a customs accord between the European Union and Turkey scrapping iron and steel duties. Turkish exports of flat and bar products to the EU were expected to rise as a result of the agreement.
"We could also meet our domestic sales target despite the cheap and low-quality steel imported from east-European countries," he added.
Eregli completed a $1.5 billion investment project this year designed to raise annual output capacity to 3.3 million tonnes from 1.5 million.
Eyuboglu said the company would reach maximum production capacity and full integration by the end of 1997.

Separately, Eregli has begun a $208 million investment programme to lower production costs, increase quality and introduce products with more added value. Eyuboglu said $56 million of the total investment would be spent in 1997 and the rest in 1998.

"This project includes investment for a fourth lime factory, modernisation of two continuous casting facilities, scrap preparation facility, expanding tin production capacity, building new docks in the new port and some power facilities," Eyuboglu said.
The agreement with the ECSC permits Eregli to expand annual output capacity to 4.5 million tonnes after the year 2000.
Eregli reported 28.95 trillion lira turnover in the first quarter of 1997 against 11.25 trillion in the same period of 1996 while its net profit increased to 2.03 trillion lira from 1.71 trillion.
